questions.q: What is the purpose of terraform import?
options: To destroy a resource and recreate it identically
To connect an existing, hand-created resource to a resource block, bringing it under Terraform's management
To copy a resource from one cloud provider to another
To back up a state file to local disk
questions.explain: terraform import lets you bring infrastructure that was created outside Terraform under its management, without destroying and recreating that resource.

questions.q: In the four-step import workflow, what must exist in your configuration BEFORE you run terraform import?
options: A fully completed resource block with every attribute already filled in
A resource block for the resource, even if it's empty
A backend block pointing at a remote state store
Nothing -- the resource block is generated automatically with no configuration
questions.explain: You need a resource block to attach the import to, even an empty one. Import connects that block's address to the real resource inside state.

questions.q: After running terraform import, what does the state file now contain that your .tf configuration might still be missing?
options: Nothing -- both are automatically kept identical after import
The resource's real current attributes, which still need to be matched by editing the .tf file until plan shows no changes
A list of every other resource in the Azure subscription
The Terraform CLI version history
questions.explain: Import only updates state with the resource's real attributes. The .tf file must still be edited to match, confirmed by running plan until it reports no changes.

questions.q: How does the Terraform 1.5+ import block differ from running terraform import on the command line?
options: It performs a completely different operation unrelated to importing resources
It achieves the same result but is written in configuration, so it runs as part of a normal plan/apply and can be reviewed in a pull request
It only works for AWS resources, never Azure
It deletes the resource from the real cloud provider
questions.explain: The import block performs the same connection as the CLI command, but because it lives in configuration, it runs through the normal plan/apply workflow and is reviewable like any other change.

questions.q: Which of these is a correct terraform import command for an Azure resource group?
options: terraform import azurerm_resource_group.example /subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/rg-northbridge-legacy
terraform apply azurerm_resource_group.example
terraform state rm azurerm_resource_group.example
terraform init -import azurerm_resource_group.example
questions.explain: terraform import takes the resource's address (type.local_name) followed by the real resource ID -- for Azure, the full /subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/... path.
